FEEDBACK: The conditional check treats shipCategory as set membership rather than the required equality: an applicable ship with both category B and category C passes because B merely exists. Enforce a single declared shipCategory with sh:maxCount 1, or revise the bounded SPARQL constraint so that, when the ice condition applies and category A is absent, any shipCategory value other than polarShipCategoryB is also a violation.

Constrain nltl:shipCategory to the supplied closed Polar Code enumeration with sh:in (nltl:polarShipCategoryA nltl:polarShipCategoryB nltl:polarShipCategoryC), while retaining the single-value and IRI checks. sh:class nltl:polarShipCategoryValue alone permits invented category individuals, so a non-applicable ship could pass with an invalid declared category.
The candidate correctly targets ships, requires the authoritative ship-owned inputs, restricts category values to A/B/C, and rejects the applicable case unless the declared category is B.
